description.value: The study examined whether intravenous ghrelin enhances neural responses to visual food cues and whether ghrelin-related brain responses are associated with subjective hunger and food-image recognition.

design.value: Twenty healthy nonobese male subjects underwent a single fMRI session 3 hr after a standardized breakfast. Twelve subjects viewed food and scenery pictures before and after ghrelin administration, while eight subjects underwent two otherwise identical saline control blocks to assess order effects.

description.value: Subjective hunger was rated on a 10 point visual analog scale before and after image blocks.
Subjective mood ratings included irritable, nauseous, and bored ratings administered at the beginning and end of each block.
Participants indicated whether each food image had been seen during scanning.
Participants rated images from 1, extremely dislike, to 9, extremely like.

task_description.value: Subjects viewed food and scenery images in two blocks, before and after intravenous ghrelin administration. Each image was shown for 5 s followed by a 15 s dark screen with a central fixation cross.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software (version 9.60, Neurobehavioral Systems, CA, USA)

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to focus their attention on the stimuli.

instrument.value: 1.5T Siemens Vision MRI scanner equipped with a quadrature radiofrequency head coil

description.value: Thirty-two 4 mm thick slices covering the whole brain were collected. The functional session consisted of six runs of 5 min, each consisting of 100 volumes per run. Two dummy images were taken at the onset of each sequence and discarded.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2* weighted images with BOLD contrast

instrument.value: 1.5T Siemens Vision MRI scanner equipped with a quadrature radiofrequency head coil

description.value: A high-resolution structural scan was obtained before functional scanning.
Functional images were spatially smoothed and motion corrected prior to statistical analyses; parametric images were transformed into Montreal Neurological Institute space.

steps.value: spatial smoothing with a 6 mm Gaussian filter
transformation into Montreal Neurological Institute space

model_settings.value: Separate regressors for food and scenery pictures, consisting of boxcar functions convolved with a standard hemodynamic response function; food minus scenery contrasts were calculated for each individual.

estimator.value: t statistic from the effect size and standard deviation of the general linear model

model_settings.value: Group analysis of individual parametric images; multiple-comparison correction used the entire brain search volume, smoothing, and degrees of freedom, listing clusters with p < 0.001 and volume greater than 100 ml.

estimator.value: t map generation and thresholding for multiple comparisons
